hook: Which launch angle sends a ball the farthest? Take a guess before you watch 👇
body: Ray the robot breaks down projectile motion in one minute: why the angle matters and how gravity bends every throw.

hook: Why do you lurch forward when a bus suddenly brakes? 🚌
body: Ray explains inertia, Newton's first law, with simple everyday examples.

hook: Why is it harder to push a heavy cart than an empty one? 🛒
body: Ray shows Newton's second law, F = m·a, step by step with a simple cart. Save this for your next physics test.
first_comment: Quick one: same push, double the mass. What happens to the acceleration? 👇

hook: When you push a wall, does the wall push back? 🧱
body: Ray reveals Newton's third law: forces always come in pairs. Send this to a friend who says 'that can't be true'.
first_comment: Who feels the bigger force: you or the wall? Tell us your answer 👇

hook: Where does a rolling ball's energy go when it stops? ⚡
body: Ray follows energy as it changes form, and shows why energy is never lost: the law of conservation of energy.
first_comment: Can you name three places the ball's energy ended up? 👇

hook: Why does a hot drink cool down but never heat up by itself? ☕
body: Ray explains heat and temperature, and why heat always flows from hot to cold. Save this for your next coffee break.
first_comment: What's the longest your coffee has ever stayed hot? ☕👇

hook: How does electricity actually get to your lamp? 💡
body: Ray follows the current through a simple electric circuit and shows what is really flowing in the wire. Send this to your favorite electrician.
first_comment: Guess first: what is actually moving inside the wire? Then check the video 👇

hook: How does the sound of a guitar reach your ear with only air in between? 🎸
body: Ray explains how waves work: they carry energy, not matter. Sound is a pressure wave, and speed = frequency × wavelength. Save this for later.
first_comment: If you could see sound waves, what sound would you look at first? 👇

hook: Why does an ambulance siren sound high coming toward you and low going away? 🚑
body: Ray explains the Doppler effect: motion squeezes and stretches waves, so the pitch changes. It works for light too. Send this to a friend who loves cars.
first_comment: Where have you noticed this? Sirens, race cars, trains? 👇
